subject: Public-source survey of Rust game population reporting and candidate implementations

findings.finding: GameDig uses Valve queries for Rust and overwrites numplayers from cp tags.
findings.implication: A GameDig-based monitor can display cp14 while a Rust browser applying the Facepunch public cap displays3.
findings.limit: This is an explanation of source differences, not evidence of Facepunch backend rules or a population fix.

findings.finding: The four retrieved Steam-user HEAD files equal installed files after newline normalization; serverQuery still maps auth_players and has the old endpoint mappings.
findings.implication: No population repair is supplied by these fetched upstream files; retain the existing exact-endpoint diagnostic adapter.
findings.limit: This checks selected HEAD files, not every branch, pull request, private fork or release.

findings.finding: The September2026 schema defines auth_players=3, players=8, query_port=2 and game_port=9 separately.
findings.implication: Do not use any field named players as a universal authenticated or Facepunch public count.
findings.limit: Schema names and numbers do not specify the Facepunch data pipeline.

findings.finding: K4RLis uses BattleMetrics plus optional Steam GetServerList; rust-servers-io fetches BattleMetrics.
findings.implication: Preserve source and cache age when comparing a third-party page to the in-game browser.
findings.limit: No deployed UI, Steam key or third-party token was used.

limitations: The survey is bounded: repository results were reviewed for relevance; not every match, fork, branch or private project was inspected.
HTTP200 is retrieval success, not proof that a search returned relevant or correctly filtered results.
Bing returned unrelated results for the attempted queries; they were excluded from technical conclusions.
Google, Jina, DuckDuckGo, Brave, Yahoo and raw.githubusercontent requests had fetch failures; selected GitHub files were instead retrieved through the public contents API at exact refs.
grep.app returned429; Sourcegraph, Mojeek and uMod returned403. No challenge, authentication or rate limit was bypassed.

Four Facepunch commit URL variants displayed the same first ten changesets rather than useful filtered results; this is not evidence that the complete official commit archive lacks player-count changes.
Three guessed wiki URLs returned404; these are not supporting sources.
Codefling public title search returned0 results for this query; the broader query was noisy. This does not exclude privately distributed or differently named plugins.
The community-plugins guidelines article inspected here does not describe player-count qualification; it must not be cited as a backend algorithm specification.
The survey found no verified public repair among inspected material; it does not prove no such implementation exists.

nextResearchQueue.acceptance: Use one owned account at a time; preserve existing sessions; require actual admission/auth observation and exact cleanup. EAC remains a separate unimplemented requirement.
